rules: Name the seven core life processes common to all living things (Nutrition, Movement, Growth, Reproduction, Respiration, Excretion, Sensitivity).
Identify main parts of a flowering plant: roots, leaves, stem, and flowers.
Explain that roots anchor the plant and absorb water, while the stem transports it.
Enforce the rule that plant growth is directly affected by temperature, light, and water variables.
life_processes_and_plants.solution_steps: 1. Identify which plant structure or life process is highlighted in the setup. 2. Reference the functional rule of that part (e.g., roots absorb water). 3. Deduce how a missing variable (like light or warmth) stops growth.

rules: Define forces simply as invisible pushes and pulls that alter an object's motion or shape.
Introduce magnets, identifying magnetic vs. non-magnetic materials (e.g., iron/steel vs. wood/plastic).
Explore how magnetic poles interact: like poles repel, opposite poles attract.
Do NOT introduce unit measurements for forces (Newtons) yet.
forces_and_magnets.solution_steps: 1. Observe the directional arrows or properties of the interacting objects. 2. Apply the rule of magnetic poles (opposite poles pull together) or force behaviors. 3. Conclude with a clear predictive motion statement.
